Recommendation

The document's committing conclusion. One per document, near the end.

Ship the OIDC migration in Q3, ahead of the vendor's September shutdown. The current SSO integration has no fallback once the vendor deprecates its legacy auth endpoint, and the two-week buffer we'd have if we start in Q4 isn't enough to catch a failed rollout before the cutoff.

Assign it to Priya's team, who already own the auth service and scoped the OIDC client work last sprint. Freeze unrelated auth changes for the two weeks around cutover.

release-gate.ts
42-if (build.passed) publish(build);
42+if (candidate.verified) publish(candidate);

The ownership boundary moves. Publication now consumes the frozen candidate that verification proved, rather than reconstructing from a build result.

Finding list

Evidence-backed review or incident findings with explicit severity, consequence, and action.

  1. High

    Verification and publication use different candidates

    Evidence. The release task rebuilds after the final validation step, so the uploaded archive is not the proven artifact.

    Consequence. A passing check cannot establish what shipped.

    Action. Freeze one candidate, verify it once, and pass that exact path to publication.

  2. Medium

    The failure receipt omits the owning stage

    Evidence. The summary reports only a final non-zero exit code.

    Action. Preserve the stage name and focused command in the receipt.

File map

A technical explanation or plan needs to show the small set of files that own behavior.

  • src/release/candidate.ts
    Owns candidate identity. Creates the immutable artifact reference passed through validation and publication.
  • src/release/verify.ts
    Owns release proof. Runs focused gates against the supplied candidate without rebuilding it.
  • src/release/publish.ts
    Owns external handoff. Uploads only the verified candidate and records the remote receipt.

Comparison grid

2-4 options side by side with best-for annotations; set data-columns to the exact option count.

Managed queue

Hosted broker, autoscaled consumers, dashboards out of the box. Fastest to stand up, least control over retry semantics.

best for: teams without spare ops bandwidth

Self-hosted worker pool

Recommended. Our own retry and backoff logic on top of a plain job table — no new infra, and we already run the failure paths we need.

best for: this migration, given our current retry requirements

Serverless functions

Pay-per-invocation, zero idle cost. Cold starts and a 15-minute execution ceiling rule out our longest ingest jobs.

best for: bursty, short-lived jobs

Timeline

Milestones, phases, or incident chronology in order; order must carry real information.

  1. Incident detected 14:02 UTC

    Error rate on checkout-service crossed the 5% alert threshold; on-call paged automatically.

  2. Root cause identified 14:19 UTC

    Bad config push to the payments gateway rejected all requests missing a new required header.

  3. Rollback in progress 14:24 UTC

    Reverting the config to the last known-good revision; checkout traffic is being shed to a static fallback in the meantime.

  4. Postmortem published pending

    Write-up due within 48 hours of resolution per the incident policy.
